title: Acids and bases - 123 school
heading: Acids and bases
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.
You learn these terms and calculations by practising. Only use BINAS when the question names a BINAS table.

questions.q: What pH does an acidic solution have?
What pH does a neutral solution have?
What pH does a basic solution have?
Which ion makes a solution acidic?
Which ion makes a solution basic?
What do you know about the number of H<sup>+</sup> and OH<sup>−</sup> ions in a neutral solution?
questions.a: There are as many H<sup>+</sup> ions as OH<sup>−</sup> ions

questions.q: Which pH is the most acidic: 2, 5, 7 or 9?
questions.a: pH 2: the lower the pH, the more acidic the solution

questions.q: What is the formula of hydrochloric acid?
What is the formula of sulfuric acid?
What is the formula of nitric acid?
What is the formula of acetic acid?
What is the formula of sodium hydroxide solution?
What is the formula of potassium hydroxide solution?
What is the formula of limewater?
What is the formula of ammonia, a base?
Which ions form when HCl dissolves in water? Write the reaction equation.
Write the reaction equation for dissolving sodium hydroxide in water.
Write the reaction equation for dissolving sulfuric acid (H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>) in water.
What is neutralisation?
questions.a: An acid reacts with a base to form a salt and water, and the pH becomes 7

questions.q: What is the reaction equation, in ions, for the neutralisation of an acid with a base?
Hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide solution. Write the reaction equation.
Sulfuric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide solution. Write the reaction equation.
Which salt forms when nitric acid (HNO<sub>3</sub>) reacts with potassium hydroxide solution (KOH)?
Zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid. Write the reaction equation.
Which gas forms when an acid reacts with a base metal, and how do you detect it?
questions.a: Hydrogen; a burning splint makes a pop

questions.q: Limestone (CaCO<sub>3</sub>) reacts with hydrochloric acid. Write the reaction equation.
What colour does litmus have in an acidic solution? (use BINAS table 36)
What colour does bromothymol blue have in a basic solution? (use BINAS table 36)
What colour does phenolphthalein have in a strongly basic solution? (use BINAS table 36)
questions.a: Purple. In an acidic or neutral solution phenolphthalein is colourless

questions.q: Universal indicator paper turns green in a solution. What kind of solution is this?
You dilute an acidic solution with a lot of water. What happens to the pH?
You add sodium hydroxide solution drop by drop to hydrochloric acid. What happens to the pH?
questions.a: The pH rises to 7 at neutralisation and then rises further

questions.q: Which hazard symbol is on a bottle of concentrated hydrochloric acid?
Why do you not get a strong acid or a strong base on your skin?
questions.a: They are corrosive and damage your skin

questions.q: How can you use an indicator to estimate the pH of a solution?
questions.a: You look at which colour the indicator has and look in BINAS table 36 to see which pH that colour belongs to
